item.title: Nancy Kassebaum, First Woman to Chair a Major Senate Panel, Dies at 94
item.description: A moderate Republican from Kansas, she served three terms before tiring of political strife. “I couldn’t get elected today,” she said in 2013.
item.dc:creator: Adam Clymer
item.media:description: Senator Nancy Kassebaum in 1995, outside her office on Capitol Hill. During the first of her three terms, she was the only woman in the Senate.

item.title: These 5 People Spent Decades Behind Bars. Here Are Their Stories.
item.description: Francis Clifford Smith, who died at 101, was among the longest-incarcerated people in the U.S. Here are some others who lived much of their lives in prison.
item.dc:creator: Amisha Padnani
item.media:description: Heirens in 1946, the year he confessed to killing two women and a 6-year-old girl.

item.title: Frank Smith, Who Served 70 Years for Murder, Dies at 101
item.description: One of the longest-serving prisoners in American history, he was sent to death row in 1950 before his sentence was commuted to life imprisonment.
item.dc:creator: Richard Sandomir

item.title: For Some in a Disrupted D.C., Grand Prix Is More Irritation Than Celebration
item.description: Race preparations have snarled traffic, rerouted flights and forced the National Gallery of Art to conduct vibration tests.
item.dc:creator: Karoun Demirjian
item.media:description: Melania Trump, the first lady, walked past an IndyCar displaying her “Be Best” slogan in the White House Rose Garden on Thursday.

item.title: Police Chief in Mississippi Regularly Used Racist Slurs, Private Text Messages Reveal
item.description: Text exchanges obtained by reporters show troubling messages sent by the chief of a Mississippi police department facing an uproar over the fatal shooting of a 1-year-old boy in June.
item.dc:creator: Mukta Joshi and Joseph Cranney
item.media:credit: Carlos Kosienski/Sipa USA, via Associated Press
item.media:description: A memorial for Kohen Wiley at the Walmart in Senatobia, Miss., in June.

item.title: How a Progressive Democrat in Florida Gave Her Party New Hope — and New Fears
item.description: Angie Nixon, a state lawmaker from Jacksonville, shocked Democrats in red Florida by soundly defeating her centrist primary opponent. Now comes the hard part.
item.dc:creator: Patricia Mazzei
item.media:credit: Saul Martinez for The New York Times
item.media:description: Representative Angie Nixon, a progressive maverick, jolted Florida politics with her upset win in the Democratic Senate primary this week.

item.title: Harry and Meghan See Their California Dreams, and Riches, Fade Away
item.description: Like so many others before them, Prince Harry and Meghan arrived in Hollywood with big plans. They are leaving with their star power fading.
item.dc:creator: Nicole Sperling and Shawn Hubler
item.media:description: The Duke and Duchess of Sussex are returning to Britain after spending six years in California chasing their Hollywood dreams.

item.title: In Ohio, Haitians Feel Shaken by Ankle Monitors and Increased ICE Presence
item.description: The devices, which will make it easier for authorities to locate immigrants in Springfield if large-scale deportations begin, have intensified a sense of dread.
item.dc:creator: Miriam Jordan
item.media:credit: Maddie McGarvey for The New York Times
item.media:description: Jonas Julien arrives at the Haitian Support Center in Springfield, Ohio, after reporting to ICE and getting fitted with an ankle monitor on Wednesday.

item.title: Why Polling Chaos Could Create Big Problems for American Politics
item.description: Bad polls. Misleading betting odds. Surveys meant to shape narratives. Ahead of the midterms and 2028, there is suddenly serious confusion about candidate strength and voter sentiment.
item.dc:creator: Reid J. Epstein
item.media:description: Polls fueled a widespread belief that Representative Haley Stevens, a moderate Democrat, was a major underdog in Michigan’s primary for Senate to Dr. Abdul El-Sayed, a progressive. She ended up losing by just a percentage point.

item.title: How the Billionaire Joe Lonsdale Shaped Trump’s Homelessness Policy
item.description: As Republicans have embraced tough measures to clear the streets, no group has led the way more than the Cicero Institute, founded by the venture capitalist Joe Lonsdale.
item.dc:creator: Ellen Barry and Jason DeParle
item.media:description: Joe Lonsdale, founder of the Cicero Institute, is an ally of President Trump’s whose group has commandeered Republican policy on homelessness.

item.title: Why the Lindsay Clancy Case Is Dividing Americans
item.description: She is being tried on murder charges for killing her three young children. The tragedy has resurrected debates over whether such women are criminals or victims.
item.dc:creator: Shaila Dewan
item.media:description: Lindsay Clancy in court during her murder trial on Wednesday in Plymouth, Mass.

item.title: With Midterms Approaching, Trump Implores Republicans: Pretend I’m on the Ballot!
item.description: President Trump was in South Carolina to stump for Darline Graham, sister of Lindsey. But his own political future was on his mind, too.
item.dc:creator: Shawn McCreesh
item.media:description: President Trump appeared at a rally with Senator Darline Graham ahead of the South Carolina Senate runoff.

item.title: Postal Service Publishes Finalized Plan to Restrict Mail Ballots
item.description: The plan, which complies with President Trump’s executive order to curtail mail voting, will only go into effect if the Supreme Court rules in the order’s favor.
item.dc:creator: Adam Sella
item.media:credit: Philip Cheung for The New York Times
item.media:description: A worker sorting ballots in 2025.

item.title: Judge Strikes Down Trump’s 75-Country Visa Ban
item.description: The ruling from the Southern District of New York found that the policy went beyond Secretary of State Marco Rubio’s legal authority.
item.dc:creator: Mattathias Schwartz
item.media:credit: Anna Watts for The New York Times
item.media:description: Travelers arriving from international flights outside the U.S. Customs and Border Protection exit at Kennedy International Airport in New York last year.

item.title: Alfalfa Sprouts Linked to Illnesses in 15 States, F.D.A. Says
item.description: Officials are investigating after multiple strains of E. coli and a type of salmonella sickened dozens of people across the United States. Two people were infected with both salmonella and E. coli.
item.dc:creator: Ishani Desai
item.category: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention
item.media:credit: St Petersburg Times/Zuma Press Wire, via Reuters
item.media:description: Public health officials have tied a number of salmonella and E. coli cases to alfalfa sprouts produced by a company in Minnesota.

item.title: Trump Accounts Get an Unlikely Endorser: Gavin Newsom
item.description: Mr. Newsom, the governor of California, normally has harsh words for President Trump. But he called the new children’s savings accounts “one of the best things” the president has done.
item.dc:creator: Laurel Rosenhall
item.media:description: Gov. Gavin Newsom of California gave an unusual endorsement for an endeavor led by President Trump — investment funds for American children born during Mr. Trump’s presidency.

item.title: Drawing on His Rust Belt Roots, Vance Campaigns for Republicans
item.description: Vice President JD Vance traveled to his hometown, Middletown, Ohio, and spoke at a steel factory where his grandfather once worked.
item.dc:creator: Zolan Kanno-Youngs
item.media:description: Vice President JD Vance spoke at a factory in Middletown, Ohio, on Friday.

item.title: Pentagon Fires Editor and Publisher of Independent Military Publication
item.description: The firings at Stars and Stripes also claimed a Middle East correspondent. They are the latest effort by the Pentagon to diminish the news outlet’s editorial independence.

item.title: Defense Rests Case in Lindsay Clancy Murder Trial
item.description: The two sides focused Friday on whether Ms. Clancy was experiencing psychosis when she strangled her three young children in 2023. Closing arguments could begin on Monday.
item.dc:creator: Sejal Govindarao and Emma Schartz
item.media:description: Lindsay Clancy in the courtroom on Thursday.

item.title: Court Slashes Award Alex Jones Was Ordered to Pay Sandy Hook Parents
item.description: An appeals court reduced the award to the parents of one victim to $6 million from $49 million, citing a Texas damages cap. The conspiracy theorist owes over $1 billion in other cases.
item.dc:creator: Elizabeth Williamson
item.media:credit: Nic Antaya for The New York Times
item.media:description: For years, Alex Jones spread conspiracy theories that the Sandy Hook shooting was a hoax perpetrated by the government and the victims’ families.

item.title: America Ends a Summer of Lightning-Fast Primaries and Political Speed Dating
item.description: Plot twists in several states have led to rapid-fire races that have felt more reminiscent of European-style snap campaigns than traditional American marathons.
item.dc:creator: Jess Bidgood
item.media:description: Senator Darline Graham and Representative Ralph Norman of South Carolina

item.title: Massachusetts’ Top Court Bars Statues of Catholic Saints at City Building
item.description: The ruling quashes a plan by the mayor of Quincy that had drawn opposition from many religious figures, as well as from residents of the racially diverse city.
item.dc:creator: Christina Morales
item.media:credit: Sophie Park for The New York Times
item.media:description: The mayor of Quincy had commissioned statues of St. Michael the Archangel and St. Florian in 2023 as the finishing touch for the city’s new public safety complex.

item.title: U.S. Agreed to Pay Liberia $5 Million in Connection with Deportees, Documents Say
item.description: The Trump administration approved the payment after Liberia said it would consider taking migrants from other countries.
item.dc:creator: Madeleine Ngo, Hamed Aleaziz and Zolan Kanno-Youngs
item.media:description: A plane carrying deportees from the United States at Roberts International Airport in Liberia on Thursday.
